fieldValues.title: The clerk's HTTP contract is one OpenAPI 3.1 document that routes, validation and client types derive from
fieldValues.decision_question: How is the contract between clerk serve and its clients kept from drifting?
fieldValues.context: Proposed from /ship clerk#96. In srs-rust, interface drift got through three gaps: embedded types emitted as {} (srs-rust#818, #1258), client types written by hand and checked only against fixtures (ADR-011), and cross-repo checks that skip when the repos are not side by side.
fieldValues.alternatives_considered: Protobuf. Schemas generated from code with golden files, as srs-rust does. Client types written by hand. Do nothing.
fieldValues.decision_statement: clerk/api/openapi.json (OpenAPI 3.1) is the single source of the service contract. The server's routes and request validation derive from it; clients generate their types from it; clerk --json outputs share its schemas. No schema is opaque ({}): SRS data refers to the canonical entity schemas. Conformance is checked against live responses, not fixtures. A breaking change needs a major version.
fieldValues.rationale: It closes each gap through which the Rust interface drifted. OpenAPI 3.1 is JSON Schema 2020-12, the dialect every SRS schema already uses, and JSON is native to the browser client; protobuf would add a second schema language.
fieldValues.revisit_when: When a client breaks on a service change that passed the gates, or a second transport (MCP) needs a contract the document cannot express.
fieldValues.next_steps: clerk#97 writes the spec first; srs-lab#7 generates the client types.
